body:
maria_support: FYI customer reporting SSO break after IdP cert rotation. Some users get 400 on POST to /saml/acs, others get 403 in app logs. Happening intermittently since yesterday afternoon.

josh_platform: thanks — can you paste the exact error the customer sees and the SP logs?

maria_support: customer screenshot shows browser POST to https://app.acme.example/saml/acs -> returns 400. They also shared our app log: 
```
2026-03-16T18:12:03Z saml: error validating assertion: recipient mismatch: expected https://app.acme.example/saml/acs but got https://app.acme.example/saml/acs/
```
(weird: trailing slash)

maria_support: repro steps from customer: 1) click "Sign in with SSO" from app 2) IdP returns SAMLResponse via POST 3) browser shows 400 and user sees "login failed". Affected ~5% of logins across regions.

josh_platform: that log points to recipient URL mismatch i.e. the Recipient in SAML assertion doesn't match our configured ACS exactly. Could be trailing slash or differing host (www vs non-www) from IdP. Ask them for the raw SAMLResponse (base64) or at least the decoded <Assertion><SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="..."> field.

maria_support: asked customer for decoded assertion. They provided sanitized fragment: 
```
<SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.acme.example/saml/acs/" NotOnOrAfter="2026-03-16T18:12:06Z"/>
```
So recipient has trailing slash. Our SP metadata lists ACS as https://app.acme.example/saml/acs (no slash).

anita_security: two possible causes: 1) strict recipient enforcement in our lib (we do exact string match) 2) cookie SameSite behavior can break POST flows if SP relies on session cookie during ACS processing (IdP POST is cross-site). Check whether cookies are being sent on the POST. If SameSite is Lax/Strict, the browser will not include cookies for cross-site POSTs.

sam_ops: I pulled the request headers from our CDN logs for two failing attempts. Key bits: 
```
POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: app.acme.example
Origin: https://idp.acme-idp.example
Cookie: (not present)
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
```
Cookie absent on the POST — so if our ACS handler expects an existing session it may treat it as anon and fail.

maria_support: customer confirmed they rotated IdP certs yesterday and changed IdP config to add a new ACS entry at the end of their metadata (they said they re-pointed to the exact path with trailing slash).

josh_platform: two separate issues then: recipient mismatch (trailing slash) and missing cookies due to SameSite policy. Short-term mitigation: 1) make recipient matching tolerant to a trailing slash OR normalize incoming Recipient URLs before checking. 2) advise customer to set the session cookie SameSite=None; Secure so cookie will be sent on cross-site POST.

anita_security: agree but note security tradeoffs for SameSite=None. Only recommend if customer accepts. Also, for cert rotation, they should publish both old and new signing certs in metadata for a rolling window. We should also accept signed assertions with either cert during rotation.

maria_support: customer asked for immediate workaround — they can 1) add a second ACS entry in their IdP metadata without trailing slash to match our SP metadata OR 2) configure the IdP to send Recipient without trailing slash. They asked if we can relax check server-side while they fix IdP.

josh_platform: I can push a quick tolerant check to staging that trims trailing slashes before comparison. But we need an ENG ticket to make canonicalization consistent across regions. Will file and assign.

saml-bot: metadata-poller: detected new metadata for tenant acme — added signing cert sha256:AB12...  (rotated 2026-03-15T22:03:00Z). Previous cert still present in metadata: yes.

maria_support: customer also reported some 403s that look signature-related. I asked them to export their metadata; they shared it — includes both certs, but the one being used to sign is the new cert. Some of our edge nodes returned: 
```
2026-03-16T18:14:10Z saml: signature verification failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (missing intermediate chain)
```
Edge region eu-west had the failures, us-east worked.

anita_security: that suggests intermediate chain missing in the IdP metadata bundle or our edge CA store didn't have the intermediate. We should check our certificate validation code: are we using system roots or bundled chain?

sam_ops: quick repro from edge node (sanitized): 
```
openssl s_client -connect idp.acme-idp.example:443 -showcerts
# server sent cert chain that omitted intermediate X
```
I think the IdP's LB is misconfigured in front of the IdP and sometimes omits the intermediate cert. That would explain region differences (different egress paths).

josh_platform: plan: 1) immediate: deploy trailing-slash-tolerant check to staging and push to canary tomorrow AM; add short-lived feature flag. 2) ask customer to add non-trailing-slash ACS entry as temp fix and set SameSite=None for session cookie if they accept. 3) open SEV-2 with eng-infra to investigate intermediate chain from IdP (we can provide openssl trace). 4) schedule metadata-poller improvement to prefer canonical ACS and log when multiple ACS differ only by slash/host alias.

maria_support: I've told customer the mitigations and asked them to add the alternate ACS and to confirm cookie policy. They preferred us making tolerant check first. They've granted permission to accept fiddling on our side for a short window.

anita_security: please log this change and add an audit entry; mark the tolerant-check rollout as reversible behind flag. Also create a playbook note for SAML cert-rotation: steps to ask customer (publish both certs, verify intermediate chain, verify ACS exactness).

josh_platform: created ENG ticket INF-2026-1127, assigned to eng-platform. Short description: "SAML: canonicalize ACS Recipient compare; add edge certificate chain checks; metadata-poller ACS normalization." Adding links and logs.

maria_support: marking this thread as escalated -> assigned to @josh_platform. Will follow up with the customer after canary deploy. :thumbsup:

josh_platform: thanks — will post canary link and rollback plan once deployed.
